question: to the Commission Yannis Maniatis (S&D) Subject:

One of the most important issues facing the Greek minority in Albania is the protection of its property rights. The Albanian Government, in addition to delaying the return of properties that had been encroached on in the past through a variety of ‘strategic investments’, especially in tourist areas, is proceeding with the expropriation of minority properties through summary procedures. On Saturday 30 May 2026, serious incidents took place in the Vlora lagoon area, where the villages of Narta and Zvërnec are located, two of the northernmost and most historical points of presence of the Greek population in Albania, during which a man of Greek descent was also injured. Residents and local organisations are reacting to the construction of a large tourist complex in the Dalani area, as one of the most important protected ecological zones on the Albanian coastline is threatened and serious land ownership issues are being raised. Bearing in mind that Albania, as a candidate country for accession, must respect the European acquis in terms of protecting both the rights of the Greek minority and the environment: 1.
Is the Commission aware of the serious incidents of last Saturday?
How is the Commission ensuring – in the context of the accession process – the protection of the rights of the Greek minority, in particular with regard to property?
Is this specific investment within a protected ecological zone compatible with European legislation and the European acquis?
answer: EN on behalf of the Commission (11.8.2026) The Commission is closely monitoring developments in Albania in the context of its EU accession process and remains in continuous contact with the Albanian authorities and civil society. In the accession process, the Commission closely follows developments related to fundamental rights, including property rights and the rights of persons belonging to minorities, as well as environmental protection. Regarding the project in the Pishë Poro–Nartë area, as with all ongoing projects in Albania, it must comply with the benchmarks under Chapter 27 (environment and climate change) of the accession negotiations. The Commission will continue to raise this issue with the Albanian authorities and underline the need for adequate environmental governance, particularly in protected areas. The Commission has so far received assurances from the Albanian authorities that a full environmental impact assessment will be carried out and that European environmental standards will be respected. The Commission will continue to closely monitor the developments regarding this and other similar large scale projects in Albania. The Commission recalls that respect for fundamental rights, including property rights and the protection of persons belonging to minorities, is an integral part of the Fundamentals Cluster 1 and is assessed throughout the accession process. Compliance with the relevant benchmarks under both the Cluster 1 and Chapter 27 will continue to be taken into account in the Commission’s overall assessment of Albania’s progress towards EU membership.
